44851Federal Register / Vol. 68, No. 146 / Wednesday, July 30, 2003 / Presidential Documents 
Executive Order 13309 of July 25, 2003
Amendments to Executive Order 12994, and Renaming the 
President’s Committee on Mental Retardation as the Presi-
dent’s Committee for People with Intellectual Disabilities 
By the authority vested in me as President by the Constitution and the 
laws of the United States of America, and in order to change the name 
of the ‘‘President’s Committee on Mental Retardation’’ to the ‘‘President’s 
Committee for People with Intellectual Disabilities’’ (the ‘‘Committee’’) and 
expand the membership of the Committee, it is hereby ordered as follows: 
Section 1. The President’s Committee on Mental Retardation is hereby re-
named the President’s Committee for People with Intellectual Disabilities. 
Sec. 2. Executive Order 12994 of March 21, 1996, is hereby amended by 
deleting the words ‘‘mental retardation’’ and inserting the words ‘‘intellectual 
disabilities’’ in lieu thereof throughout the text of that order, except in 
the title, the first line of the preamble, and section 1 of that order. 
Sec. 3. Section 1 of Executive Order 12994 is amended by deleting the 
words ‘‘(the ‘‘Committee’’)’’ and adding after ‘‘responsibilities,’’ the words 
‘‘and renamed the President’s Committee for People with Intellectual Disabil-
ities (the ‘‘Committee’’),’’. 
Sec. 4. Section 2 of Executive Order 12994 is amended by inserting after 
‘‘(5) The Secretary of Housing and Urban Development;’’ the following: 
‘‘(6) The Secretary of Commerce; (7) The Secretary of Transportation; (8) 
The Secretary of the Interior; (9) The Secretary of Homeland Security;’’ 
and renumbering former subsections (6) through (9) as subsections (10) 
through (13). 
Sec. 5. The Committee is continued until September 30, 2005.
W
THE WHITE HOUSE, 
July 25, 2003. 
[FR Doc. 03–19572
Filed 7–29–03; 8:57 am]

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Sec. 1 of this order ("The President’s Committee on Mental Retardation is hereby renamed the President’s Committee for People with Intellectual Disabilities.") renamed the committee. The renaming took effect when the order was signed on 2003-07-25 and no end is stated in the clause or elsewhere in the order. Its result is still the current text of the order it amended: EO 13446 sec. 5 restates EO 12994 so that the committee "renamed the President’s Committee for People with Intellectual Disabilities (Committee), is hereby continued in operation", and the U.S. Code note to 42 U.S.C. 15001 (release point 119-121, current through 2026-10-09) prints EO 12994 as amended by EO 13309 (68 F.R. 44851) and by EO 13446 sec. 5 (72 F.R. 56176); that note is a lead read through the bounded U.S. Code search, not a cited basis. Before the restatement the clause named the committee in the rename; after it the restated sec. 1 of EO 12994 repeats the new name, so the substance of the rename is preserved. operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Sec. 5 says "The Committee is continued until September 30, 2005." The date is the stated end of this command and is recorded inclusive (the continuance runs through the end of 2005-09-30); on the exclusive reading it ended when that day began. Nothing in the order extends it. The committee was later continued by separate orders each with its own date and terms; EO 13446 sec. 1(g) (signed 2007-09-28, effective 2007-09-30) lists "President’s Committee for People with Intellectual Disabilities; Executive Order 12994, as amended" among the committees "continued until September 30, 2009", which is a new continuance by a later order and not an extension of this clause, which is why this clause is recorded as terminated on its own stated date while the committee itself continues under other commands.
